title: Incident bot context bundle — MVP notes (working doc)
content:
Owner: Rafa (SRE)
Doc purpose: capture MVP definition + what responders find useful vs noisy. This is intentionally messy; we’ll distill into the Confluence spec + runbook.

Last updated: 2025-02-25

---

1) Why we’re doing this (quick context)
- We keep losing the first ~10–20 minutes in incidents chasing “what changed?” and “where is it saturated?”
- Goal is for the bot to post a context bundle in the first 2–5 minutes that materially reduces time-to-suspect-change.
- Primary incidents where this helps: latency regressions, 5xx spikes, 429/throttling bursts, region-specific degradation, bad rollout/config.

Non-goals for MVP
- Bot taking actions (no auto rollback, no autoscaling changes)
- Posting raw logs or customer payloads (hard no)
- Perfect root cause detection (we just need “strong clues” fast)

---

2) MVP definition (what the bot must do)
MVP = a single message (or a small set of messages, but not spam) in the incident thread that answers:
A) Did anything relevant change recently? (deploys, rollouts, config)
B) Are we saturated somewhere? (queue depth / throttling / GPU pressure signals)
C) Where do I click next? (canonical dashboards + runbook links)

Hard requirements (MVP)
- Posts automatically when:
  - an incident is created in #incidents (or via PagerDuty -> Slack bridge)
  - a Sev-0/Sev-1 alert fires with incident thread created
- Completes in <= 60s typical, <= 120s p95 (fail open; partial bundle ok)
- Region-aware: if incident is tagged us-east, don’t show only global aggregates
- Redaction / safe-to-post classification for config diffs (must be conservative)
- If data is missing, bot must say “missing because X” (metrics lag / timeout) not silently omit

MVP collectors (in order)
1) Recent deploys / rollouts (per service + region)
2) Config diffs (effective routing policy + flags; allowlist keys)
3) Saturation snapshot (top signals + link to dashboard)

Nice-to-haves (post-MVP)
- “Suspected change” heuristic (highlight overlap with degradation window)
- Canary awareness (percent, stage, targeted cohorts)
- Per-route SLO panel deep links (auto-generated based on incident service)

---

3) Proposed default time windows (tentative)
This came up a lot in #eng-oncall poll.

Current proposal
- Deploy collector:
  - show last 2 deploy events OR last 60 minutes, whichever is smaller (per service/region)
  - include rollbacks/hotfixes as first-class events
- Config diff collector:
  - compare t-30m vs now (for effective config), but allow responder command to widen to t-2h
- Saturation collector:
  - show “now” snapshot and a 15m trend (sparklines or min/max) if easy

Command overrides (future)
- /incident-bot context --window 120m
- /incident-bot deploys --service router --region us-east

Open question: how often should bot re-post?
- leaning: initial bundle + one refresh at +10m only if incident is still active AND signals changed materially

---

4) Slack formatting: readability rules (what’s working)
General
- One top-line summary per section, then optionally “details” collapsed.
- Prefer small tables / aligned columns; avoid big JSON blobs.
- Always show timestamps with timezone (UTC) and relative age.
- Put links at end of section (dashboards/runbook) so the top stays scannable.

Must not do
- Post 10+ messages in the thread.
- Dump raw diffs with 200 lines.
- Include request payloads, prompts, tokens, customer identifiers.

---

5) Examples: “good” vs “noisy” bundles

5.1 GOOD bundle example (what responders liked)
(Example text; not exact output)

[Context bundle v0.1] Incident: INC-1843 | Service: inference-router | Region: us-east | Window: last 60m

1) Recent deploys (us-east)
- 12:41 UTC (17m ago) inference-router v2.18.7 (canary 10%)  → GitHub PR 18421 | Release run #8421
- 12:12 UTC (46m ago) inference-router v2.18.6 (100%)        → GitHub PR 18398 | Release run #8412
Notes: canary currently enabled; cohort = “enterprise-small”
Links: Deploy timeline (Grafana) | Release pipeline

2) Config diffs (effective policy, t-30m → now)
Changed keys (safe-to-post):
- routing.fallback_model: "mistral-7b" → "mixtral-8x7b"
- rate_limits.default_rps: 950 → 800
- autoscaling.max_replicas: 64 → 48
No changes detected in: auth.*, customer_overrides.*, secrets.*
Links: Config snapshot diff view | Runbook: triage with deploy+config context

3) Saturation snapshot (us-east, last 15m)
- GPU queue depth: P95 210 (HIGH) | baseline ~40
- Scheduler contention: 0.78 (HIGH) | baseline ~0.25
- Throttling (429): 3.2% of requests (HIGH)
Links: Saturation dashboard | 429 drilldown | Router latency SLO

What made this good:
- Small number of deploys.
- Config diff is “just the important keys” + explicitly notes what was not checked.
- Saturation is 3 signals max and clearly labeled HIGH/baseline.
- Lots of links, but placed after scannable facts.


5.2 NOISY bundle example (what we should avoid)

[Context bundle]
- deploys: 23 events (lists every microservice deploy for the last 6h)
- config: full JSON diff (includes customer_override map keys, opaque ids)
- saturation: 18 metrics with unlabeled units and no region scoping
- posts as 7 messages in thread within 30 seconds

Responder feedback:
- “This is just more scrolling; I can’t find the likely culprit.”
- “Please stop printing config keys that look sensitive even if they’re not.”
- “I don’t know which of these metrics actually matters.”

---

6) Early responder feedback snippets (from incidents + on-call threads)

From #incidents thread 1706831123_104455 (deploy context request)
- “If the bot can just tell me what shipped in the last hour for *this* service + region, I’ll be happy.”
- “Include canary % if possible; canary vs 100% matters a lot in decision making.”

From #incidents thread 1706904450_883102 (config diff gap)
- “Routing changes are the most common footgun; diff the effective policy, not the source file in git.”
- “We need a clear ‘safe-to-post’ boundary. When in doubt, post less and link to restricted view.”

From #eng-oncall poll 1707059911_552901 (time window/noise)
- “2 deploys is enough; 10 deploys is noise.”
- “Default window should be 60m; if it’s older we can ask for more.”

From #incidents thread 1707764888_452019 (metrics lag / partial failures)
- “If saturation is missing, say it’s missing. Silence looks like ‘no saturation’ which is dangerous.”
- “Partial bundle is fine, but include per-section error messages and retry hint.”

---

7) Redaction + restricted mode notes (security concerns)
Working assumptions (need security sign-off; Marcus reviewing)
- Config diffs must be allowlist-only for MVP.
- Never post:
  - customer identifiers, org ids, request hashes
  - auth config, tokens, KMS info, secret names/paths
  - customer_override maps (even if values are benign)
- Bot must support “restricted incident” mode:
  - Minimal info in #incidents (high-level + links)
  - Full bundle only in restricted channel (allowlist) OR in incident tool UI

Open question: do we need redaction audit log in MVP or can it be Phase 2?
- SRE preference: at least minimal audit trail (what keys were removed and why) somewhere non-Slack.

---

8) MVP success criteria (informal, for now)
We’ll formalize in the metrics doc.
- 70%+ of Sev-0/1 incidents get a bundle posted within 2 minutes (excluding Slack downtime etc.)
- 50%+ of incidents have “suspected change” identified by responders within 10 minutes (baseline tbd)
- On-call qualitative: responders mark bundle “useful” more than “noisy” in feedback reactions
- Bot reliability: <1% hard failure where nothing posts; collectors time out rather than hanging

---

9) Open questions / TODOs
Format + content
- Do we put saturation before config diff? (some responders start from “are we saturated?”)
- Should we show “no recent deploys” explicitly? (yes, likely)
- How to show multi-region incidents: one combined table vs separate sections per region?

Data sources
- Source of truth for “effective config snapshot”: API call vs event-sourced snapshot
- How to map deploy events to service names consistently (Connor + Infra thread)
- Canary metadata: where do we get % and cohort? release pipeline schema changes?

Guardrails
- Caching/memoization keyed by incident + window (avoid hammering config API)
- Concurrency limits per collector to avoid cascading issues during major incident
- Rate limiting on Slack posting (and re-post refresh behavior)

---

10) Next steps (near-term)
- Jacob: implement collector scaffolding + timeouts + partial bundle rendering (ENG-2845)
- Connor: deploy event payload improvements (include canary %) + naming consistency
- Mina/Ethan: config snapshot endpoint performance + caching; clarify allowlisted keys
- Allison/Logan: pick 3–5 saturation signals for MVP and define HIGH thresholds; ensure region labels
- Rafa/Sean: run a mini game-day with synthetic latency spike + deploy during incident; collect feedback

Notes to self (Rafa)
- When we share this broadly, emphasize the bot is an assistant, not a source of truth.
- Add a simple thumbs up/down + “too noisy / missing data / wrong region” quick feedback control.
